6. γε [at least] joined with prepositions
γε [at least] in replies serves either to confirm or to define more precisely the statement
where the verse of the other person which had preceded has fallen out.

γε [at least] joined with other particles either precedes or follows, of which kind are γε μὲν δή [at least indeed], γε μέντοι [at least however], γε μήν [at least truly], ἀλλὰ γε [but at least], ἀλλὰ μήν γε [but truly at least], ἀτὰρ – γε [but – at least], δέ γε and δὲ γε [and at least], καὶ γε [and at least], καὶ μὴν γε [and truly at least], μέντοι γε [however at least] and others. About all these it has been said under those particles with which it is actually joined, and more examples are found in the passages cited above. But wrongly οὐκ ἄν γ' [not at least] is in some copies at Ag. 340, in others the simple οὐκ ἄν [not], (for in M this part of the play has fallen out), but Hermann restored the correct reading οὔ τἄν [not then].
